newsitem.title: UK: LME copper firm above $2,200 in late trading.
newsitem.headline: LME copper firm above $2,200 in late trading.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices spiked higher in late trading as nearby spreads widened.
Also aiding the move was a break above $2,200 which encouraged short-covering and broker covering ahead of Tuesday's LME inventory data.
Stocks are expected to fall slightly.

"Tomorrow's stock figure as ever is the market's key focus point as the debate continues on the ultimate destination of the material withdrawn from the LME warehouses of late," LME brokers Rudolf Wolff said.
Three months delivery was hovering near at $2,215 by 1900 GMT, up on its earlier levels of around $2,200.
The cash to three months backwardation after narrowing in to $145 earlier moved to settle at $175.
Traders noted a move by the London Clearing House (LCH) to raise copper's cash to three months spread margin. The LCH said the spread margin was raised to $3,750 from $1,875.
This action should deter fundamental tightness from being further exacerbated by speculative activity, sources said.
"It will help to prevent a speculative accumulation on top," one said.
Though stocks are expected to fall on Tuesday several traders suggest that they could start to rise over the coming weeks.
Elsewhere, other base metals remained quiet but clawed higher in line with copper's late move.
